scope: Actual original provider word timings. Speech and holds preserved by the case-construction repair.

beats.say: Article six has two high-risk routes. The product route requires both an Annex one product or its safety component, and the relevant third-party conformity assessment for health and safety. Solely non-safety assistance, efficiency or convenience does not make a safety component. Failure that endangers health and safety can. A conformity check solely for unrelated risks does not satisfy the second condition. Preserve both inputs of this AND test.

Annex three is a separate listed-use route. It includes specified biometrics, educational assessment, employment and essential-service decisions. Its creditworthiness entry expressly excludes financial-fraud detection. For a supplied intake, distinguish an applicant's creditworthiness decision from a transaction-fraud detector, then check other applicable duties. A model swap leaves the applicant decision's intended use intact.

The Annex three exception requires no significant risk to health, safety or fundamental rights, including no material influence on decision outcomes. At least one of four conditions must also apply. These are a narrow procedural task, improving a completed human activity, detecting decision patterns or deviations without replacing or influencing the completed assessment without proper human review, or a preparatory task. A provider relying on it documents the assessment before marketing or service and registers the system. Annex three profiling of natural persons remains high risk despite that exception test.

For covered high-risk systems, Articles nine through fifteen concern risk management, data governance, documentation, logging, transparency, human oversight, accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity. Check the responsible actor and sector route. Article two gives Annex one Section B products a special integration regime through sector legislation. The same direct compliance checklist does not fit every regulated product. Our promotion assistant's local controls do not by themselves declare it an Annex three high-risk system.

Keep the general-purpose model layer visible below the application. Article fifty-three covers technical model documentation, information for downstream integrators, a copyright policy and a sufficiently detailed public summary of training content. Qualifying open-source models have a limited exception from the first two duties, not from copyright policy or the public summary. That exception does not apply to models with systemic risk.

Articles fifty-one and fifty-two address high-impact capabilities and Commission designation. More than ten to the twenty-fifth training FLOPs creates a presumption of high-impact capabilities, with an exceptional rebuttal procedure. It is not the only route: the Commission can designate a model based on equivalent capabilities or impact under the specified criteria. Being below the compute threshold alone does not prove the model is outside systemic-risk duties.

Article fifty-five adds state-of-the-art model evaluation and documented adversarial testing, assessment and mitigation of Union-level systemic risks, serious-incident reporting and cybersecurity. Known or estimated training energy consumption belongs in Annex eleven documentation under Article fifty-three; that is not a separate energy-efficiency duty unique to systemic-risk models. The model provider's documentation helps an integrator, while the integrator still assesses its application's intended use, permissions and affected people.

Protect the measurement that feeds the gate. The first risk row covers unauthorized promotion. A second row covers contaminated evaluation evidence: holdout leakage into training, correct answers exposed through agent-readable harness paths, and judge prompt injection. Any can inflate a score while leaving the candidate unsafe. The evaluation and release owner owns this risk separately from the authorization implementation.

Isolate holdout content from training and agent-readable paths, and treat judge inputs as untrusted. Check exact and near-duplicate overlap, audit harness access, attack the judge and swap candidate order. Block release on known leakage. Once a failed held-out example guides a repair, label it a seen development regression rather than claiming it is still untouched evidence. A new private evaluation tests generalization; success on the repaired case tests that repair.

The system card describes what shipped: model snapshot, prompts, policies, enabled tools, effect gates, tests, limitations and rollback owner. The dataset record describes the cases that produced a score: provenance, labeling, sensitive fields, split and retention. A schema can catch blanks and missing lists while saying nothing about label quality, actual evaluation execution or retention enforcement. A dataset version or labeling change must remain linked to the matching report and accepted deployment evidence.

Evaluate the actual effect of each trace. Our first supplied suite contains a forbidden promotion and an unnecessarily blocked legitimate request. Attack success and false rejection use different denominators. The release gate reports both findings as separate findings.

Replace those outcomes with a supplied successful retest. The local effect and friction predicates pass. A tiny suite still leaves substantial uncertainty. The displayed zero-failure bound assumes independent trials from a fixed distribution; curated attacks usually serve as targeted failure probes.

Remove the benign cases and coverage becomes unknown. An empty denominator supplies no false-rejection estimate. Keep case identities, evaluation version and remediation owner to establish which behavior was checked.

Reconstruct the rates: attack success is forbidden effects divided by attack traces, while false rejection is wrongly blocked eligible requests divided by eligible requests. The first suite gives one third and one half. With zero observed failures in three independent fixed-distribution trials, the exact one-sided ninety-five-percent upper bound is one minus point zero five to the power one third, about sixty-three point two percent. Targeted curated attacks are not that random sample. Preserve seen development regressions separately from held-out evaluation.

Now make the appeal path concrete. C seventeen was held at ten percent because its required security review was missing. The owner receives that reason, the policy version and a usable challenge reference. A reviewer who took no part in the original decision opens the original proposal, evaluation package, policy and configuration versions, approval receipts and effect record. The empty effect ledger confirms that the proposal did not move traffic in this constructed replay.

The reviewer first reconstructs the original decision under the policy then in force. If the security review really was absent, uphold that hold and explain what evidence is needed. If a valid, authorized receipt already covered that exact proposal but the gate failed to read it, record a factual correction and assign the gate defect. The historical hold stays in the log. A later policy change is a new basis for a new decision, not a rewrite of Monday's facts.

A newly supplied approval can complete the current case only if it is authoritative, fresh, unrevoked and bound to the current candidate, environment, target, policy and evidence. Revalidate at the executor boundary so the proposal cannot change between check and effect. An appeal result or APPROVED FOR EXECUTOR is not an executed promotion. Record the actual effect separately; a lost response leaves an uncertain outcome that needs reconciliation before retry.

Effective oversight gives people time, evidence, expertise and authority to disagree, override within their remit or halt safely. Article fourteen for covered high-risk systems addresses understanding limitations, automation bias, interpreting output, overriding it and safe intervention. A person's name on an org chart does not supply those abilities. Appeal outcomes can point to bad data, unclear policy, missing evidence or an explanation that needs repair.

The local appeal is an organizational control. Article eighty-six has a narrower legal scope: a deployer decision based on an Annex three high-risk system, excluding point two, must produce legal or similarly significant effects considered adverse to health, safety or fundamental rights. The right concerns a clear, meaningful explanation of the AI role and main decision elements, subject to lawful exceptions or restrictions and only where that right is not otherwise provided by Union law. Assess its applicability separately; our promotion case does not automatically establish it.

Try a new case. Candidate C twenty-nine has complete accepted evidence and fresh release and security approvals for a ten-percent target with an untrusted note. The policy, artifact and evaluation versions match. Hold the calculation: change only its target to fifteen percent. Can the ten-percent approvals and old deployment evidence authorize this proposal? Keep the traffic ledger empty while you decide.

They cannot. The exact proposal binding changes, and fifteen is above ten, so our local rule also requires exception review. Revalidate the changed scope and collect the affected current evidence and authoritative receipts. One successful poisoned-note replay does not replace the complete reviewed package, benign coverage or open-findings checks. The old ten-percent decision remains valid as a historical record for its own scope.

If C twenty-nine's owner disputes this new hold, the independent reviewer sees both versions and the precise changed field. A correction can fix a misread receipt; it cannot stretch an approval to a scope it never covered. You can now trace a harm to an owner, a tested control, the actual evidence, a protected decision record and a challenge that can change the outcome while preserving what happened.

Bring the records together around one candidate. The draft lacks its dataset record and retains open findings, so the gate identifies those gaps. Each reviewed artifact must match the candidate and the digest of its actual deployment configuration.

Supply the complete reviewed package and closed findings. The local candidate becomes eligible for release approval. These inputs represent authenticated review outcomes in our fixture. Product operation, legal duties and deployment authorization retain their own evidence and decision owners.

Change the policy with the same candidate name. The manifest digest changes, and the old reviews stop matching. Governance works through this continuous connection: people and purpose, owned risks, tested controls, preserved decisions and evidence that remains valid for the system being released.

Name the eight artifacts: workflow memo, risk row, system card, dataset record, audit replay, red-team report, accessibility and slice report, and oversight runbook. Bind each accepted review to the exact candidate and deployment digest over model, prompt, policy, tools, evaluation and environment. Required legal signoff and zero remaining unsafe-effect and accessibility findings are separate predicates. The host computes the actual digest. Supplied accepted Booleans in our simulation stand for authenticated review outcomes; the author cannot certify the evidence by setting them true.
